symbols.name: digit width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each digit of an input; the radix is $2^\varpi$.
symbols.quote: Let $\varpi$ be the digit width, the number of bits in each digit, and let $2^\varpi$ be the radix, the base of the digits.

symbols.name: digit count
symbols.meaning: The number of digits in each input, which is $\lceil n/\varpi\rceil$.
symbols.quote: Let $\Upsilon = \lceil n/\varpi\rceil$ be the digit count, the number of digits in each input.

symbols.name: digit of an input
symbols.meaning: The digit of $x$ (or $y$) at a position, a value from $0$ to $2^\varpi-1$.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathrm{dig}_i(x)$ be the digit of $x$ at position $i$, for $0 \le i \le \Upsilon-1$, where positions are counted from 0 at the least significant end, so that $x = \sum_{i=0}^{\Upsilon-1} \mathrm{dig}_i(x)\,(2^\varpi)^i$.

symbols.name: formal variable
symbols.meaning: A symbol that is not a number, in which the digit polynomials are written.
symbols.quote: Let $\vartheta$ be a formal variable, a symbol that is not a number.

symbols.name: digit polynomial of x
symbols.meaning: The polynomial in $\vartheta$ whose coefficients are the digits of $x$.

symbols.name: digit polynomial of y
symbols.meaning: The polynomial in $\vartheta$ whose coefficients are the digits of $y$.

symbols.name: digit position in x
symbols.meaning: A position of a digit of $x$, counted from 0 at the least significant end, from 0 to $\Upsilon-1$.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathrm{dig}_i(x)$ be the digit of $x$ at position $i$, for $0 \le i \le \Upsilon-1$, where positions are counted from 0 at the least significant end, so that $x = \sum_{i=0}^{\Upsilon-1} \mathrm{dig}_i(x)\,(2^\varpi)^i$.

symbols.name: digit position in y
symbols.meaning: A position of a digit of $y$, counted from 0 at the least significant end, from 0 to $\Upsilon-1$.
symbols.quote: The digits $\mathrm{dig}_j(y)$ of $y$ are defined the same way, with $j$ the position of a digit counted from 0; this changes $j$ from its meaning on [Integer](integer.md).

symbols.name: coefficient index
symbols.meaning: The index of a coefficient of the product of the digit polynomials, running from $0$ to $2\Upsilon-2$.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathrm{cv}_\varsigma$ be the coefficient of $\vartheta^\varsigma$ in the product $\hat{x}(\vartheta)\hat{y}(\vartheta)$, where the coefficient index $\varsigma$ runs over $0 \le \varsigma \le 2\Upsilon-2$.

symbols.name: convolution coefficient
symbols.meaning: The coefficient of $\vartheta^\varsigma$ in the product of the digit polynomials, an entry of the convolution of the digit sequences.
symbols.quote: Let $\mathrm{cv}_\varsigma$ be the coefficient of $\vartheta^\varsigma$ in the product $\hat{x}(\vartheta)\hat{y}(\vartheta)$, where the coefficient index $\varsigma$ runs over $0 \le \varsigma \le 2\Upsilon-2$.

symbols.name: transform length
symbols.meaning: The power-of-two length of the transform, at least $2\Upsilon-1$ and below $4\Upsilon$.
symbols.quote: The convolution is computed with the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) at a power-of-two length $\mathcal{T}$ of at least $2\Upsilon-1$.

relations.quote: Radix-digit convolution is a reduction of [Exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) to a convolution of short integer coefficients, obtained by writing each input as a polynomial in a power of two whose coefficients are its digits.
The convolution is computed with the [Discrete Fourier transform](discrete-fourier-transform.md) at a power-of-two length $\mathcal{T}$ of at least $2\Upsilon-1$.

Radix-digit convolution computes its transforms from [Butterfly](butterfly.md) operations: each level applies a butterfly to each pair of positions whose indices differ in one bit, so a transform of length $\mathcal{T}$ has $\log_2 \mathcal{T}$ levels.
Radix-digit convolution states its bounds in [Big-Theta notation](big-theta-notation.md), so the costs below are $\Theta$ bounds.
